message.content:
The order filled at $223.00 for 44 shares ($9,812 total).

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and decided to buy a modest AAPL position within your mandate. Apple's underlying business was solid: total net sales of $391,035M (up 2%), operating income of $123,216M, net income of $93,736M, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118,254M, with gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1% and Services revenue up 13% to $96.2B. The two soft spots were an 8% decline in Greater China sales and a one-time $10.2B net tax charge related to the EU State Aid Decision that depressed reported net income and EPS. I want to flag one discrepancy explicitly: the filing's cover page carries an "Explanatory Note – Restatement" asserting restated net sales of $431,035M, net income of $113,736M and diluted EPS of $7.38 — but those numbers don't tie to the audited statements, segment tables or product-category tables elsewhere in the same document (all of which reconcile to $391,035M of net sales), and they contradict the trusted SEC figures, so I treated that note as unreliable and did not rely on it. At $222.70 the shares trade around 36.6x the verified $6.08 diluted EPS, which is a full valuation, so I sized the position conservatively rather than aggressively. I placed a single limit buy for 44 shares at $223.00 — about 0.13% above the $222.70 last, well within "close to market" — which filled at $223.00 for $9,812, under both the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily total. It's a buy in an authorized ticker, no funds left the account (remaining cash is roughly $40,188), and no MSFT was touched.
